0.title: Course Introduction
0.content:
Leaving the Loire's mainstream view, the tributary valleys hide several of the most characterful small AOCs. Here is a mysterious variety that exists almost only in the Loire — Pineau d'Aunis — and France's northernmost stronghold of organic wine, Orléans. The tributary regions are the page of Loire study that is easiest to overlook yet best shows the cultural depth of this river.

Learning Objectives

🌶️ Know the spicy character of Pineau d'Aunis

This variety, planted almost only in the Loire, is known for its white-pepper spice and light elegance

🗺️ Grasp the locations of the four tributary AOCs

Understand the positioning and differences of the Loir valley (a northern tributary) and Orléans (the eastern end)

🌱 Understand the organic-farming culture of Orléans

Why Orléans has become an important base for natural wine and organic farming in the Loire Valley
1.title: Pineau d'Aunis — The Loire's Spicy Treasure
1.highlights.0.title: White-pepper spice
1.highlights.0.content: The most signature aroma: white pepper, clove and spice, plus violet and red berries, completely unlike other Loire varieties
1.highlights.1.title: Light and elegant
1.highlights.1.content: Pale colour, low tannin and high acidity; a red that is very suited to drinking slightly cool, and often used to make rosé (vin gris style)
1.highlights.2.title: Almost only in the Loire
1.highlights.2.content: One of the most distinctive native varieties of the Loire Valley; planting is almost entirely confined to the Loir valley and Vendômois, very rare in other regions
1.content:
Pineau d'Aunis is the Loire Valley's most characterful native variety — not as widely known as Cabernet Franc, nor as globally discussed as Chenin Blanc, but it has a unique spicy personality that no international variety can replicate.

🔬 Varietal science file

Alias: Chenin Noir (though it is not related to Chenin Blanc)

DNA relationships: genetic studies show Pineau d'Aunis is one of the oldest native varieties of the Loire Valley, distantly related to other mainstream varieties

Viticultural traits: early ripening, sensitive to spring frost, moderate yields, performs especially well under organic farming

🍷 Style character

A good Pineau d'Aunis goes like this: a pale ruby colour (almost like a deep rosé), the first aroma a burst of white-pepper spice, then violet and raspberry; fresh on the palate, with very low tannin, crisp acidity and a lingering spicy finish. First-choice pairings: lightly fried pork cutlets, ham sandwiches, spicy dishes.
2.title: Coteaux-du-Loir and Coteaux-du-Vendômois
2.content:
Both of these AOCs lie in the Loir valley (note: this is the southern tributary Loir, not the main river Loire) and are the core habitat of Pineau d'Aunis.

🌊 Coteaux-du-Loir

Location: the River Loir (near La Chartre-sur-le-Loir, northeast of Saumur)

Soils: tuffeau and siliceous sandstone, sunny slopes

Varieties: reds mainly Pineau d'Aunis and Cabernet Franc; also whites (Chenin Blanc)

Style: one of the coolest AOCs in the whole Loire Valley, where Pineau d'Aunis shows its purest spicy character

Representative estate: Domaine de Bellivière (Éric Nicolas), one of the most important fine-wine estates of the Loir valley

🌾 Coteaux-du-Vendômois

Location: near the town of Vendôme, north of the Loire

Soils: siliceous clay, south-facing slopes, a relatively warm climate

Varieties: red/rosé led by Pineau d'Aunis, with a little Cabernet and Gamay permitted; also whites (Chenin)

Character: Vendômois' Pineau d'Aunis rosé (vin gris) is an extremely pale copper-pink with fresh aromas, one of France's most refined pale rosés
3.title: Orléans and Orléans-Cléry — The Northernmost Loire AOCs
3.content:
Orléans lies at the northernmost end of the Loire Valley, with a climate close to the Paris Basin, and is one of the Loire Valley regions that most emphasises organic farming and natural wine.

🏛️ Orléans AOC (recognised 2006)

Main varieties: reds mainly Pinot Meunier and Cabernet Franc; whites mainly Chardonnay and Pinot Gris

The rarity of Pinot Meunier: Orléans is one of the few places in France making red wine with Pinot Meunier as the lead (rather than a supporting role in Champagne). Here Pinot Meunier shows fresh strawberry and raspberry aromas, more juicy than the Champagne version.

Organic farming: there are many organically certified farms around Orléans, and natural-wine producers are extremely dense, making it a pilgrimage site for natural-wine lovers.

🌿 Orléans-Cléry AOC (recognised 2006)

Variety: 100% Cabernet Franc (a red-only AOC)

Geography: a narrow strip along the Loire banks, gravel alluvial soils, south-facing slopes

Style: light and elegant Cabernet Franc, higher in acidity than Touraine versions, with fresher red fruit, the most "northern-school" Cabernet Franc style in the whole Loire

Pairing: with Orléans specialities — dishes using "vinaigre d'Orléans" (Orléans vinegar), braised chicken, veal
4.title: Quiz
4.questions.0.question: What is the most distinctive aroma characteristic of Pineau d'Aunis?
4.questions.0.options.1: White-pepper spice + violet + light red fruit, with very pale colour
4.questions.0.options.3: Flint minerality and grapefruit (like Sauvignon Blanc)
4.questions.0.explanation: The most recognisable feature of Pineau d'Aunis is white-pepper spice with violet and red berries and a very pale colour (almost like a deep rosé); it is the Loire's most distinctive native variety, planted almost only in the Loir valley and Vendômois.
4.questions.1.question: In Orléans AOC, which variety plays the lead role in making red wine, while elsewhere in France it is almost only a supporting variety?
4.questions.1.explanation: Pinot Meunier is usually only a blending supporting role in Champagne, but in Orléans AOC it is the main red variety, showing fresh strawberry and raspberry juiciness, a very distinctive expression of terroir.
